title: CI: run both test suites on every push and pull request
intent: This repository has no .github/workflows/ at all, so nothing runs either suite on a push and every green number in HANDOFF.md §5 came from a human running tests by hand. That is not a theoretical gap: on a fresh container both suites are red until someone runs `npm ci`, because node_modules is absent in the repository root and in toy/ alike, and nothing in the repo asserts the install step. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on push to any branch and on pull_request, installs dependencies with `npm ci` in the repository root AND in toy/ (both have a committed package-lock.json), then runs the root suite (`npm test`, expected 105 passing) and the toy suite (`cd toy && npm test`, expected 60 passing) as separately named steps so a reader can tell which one failed. Pin actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to a major version tag and set node-version to 20 to match the engines field in package.json. The job must fail when either suite fails. Do not add linting, coverage, matrix builds, caching, deployment, or any release automation — this item is the missing verification step and nothing else.

title: Deliver a gate to a human: a pluggable, best-effort notifier beside `gates.js open`
intent: Nothing delivers a gate to a human. `substrate/gates.js` writes a JSON file and exits; `grep -n "notif|alert|webhook|slack|email" substrate/gates.js` returns nothing. The measured cost: run m1 emitted a sev1 page at 2026-09-11T03:04:00Z that was opened 18h53m later, and only because a human happened to ask for a Phase 4 audit. Nothing about the silence distinguished 'no sev1' from 'an unmitigated sev1 nobody has been told about'. Build a notifier that runs beside `gates open`, never inside a workflow, because a workflow cannot pause for a person and the gate record is already the single place every page passes through. Hard requirements: (1) Delivery is BEST-EFFORT AND NON-BLOCKING — a failed, timed-out or unconfigured send must never fail the gate, never change the exit code of `gates open`, and never prevent the record being written; the record on disk stays the source of truth and the notification is a pointer to it. (2) The GateRecord must record that delivery was ATTEMPTED and whether it SUCCEEDED, so an unopened page is distinguishable from an undelivered one — which is exactly what could not be told apart for m1. Add a `delivery` object to the GateRecord $def in contracts.schema.json carrying at minimum attempted (boolean), ok (boolean), channel (string), at (ISO string) and error (string, optional); it must be optional so all 18 existing records in gates/closed/ still validate. (3) Severity routes: a sev1_page and a budget breach go to the phone channel; a spec_gate and other routine gates go to the queue channel. The routing table is code, not configuration guesswork. (4) The transport is PLUGGABLE — a driver interface with the driver selected by environment variable. Ship exactly one driver that is verified end-to-end from this container: a GitHub issue driver that opens a labelled issue via the GitHub REST API using a token read from the environment. This is the only reachable transport: the organisation egress policy answers 403 at CONNECT for ntfy.sh, hooks.slack.com, api.pushover.net, api.telegram.org and api.twilio.com, while api.github.com answers 200. A generic webhook driver MAY be included for the operator to point at ntfy or Slack from their own machine, but it must be documented in substrate/README.md as UNVERIFIED FROM CI, and no test may claim otherwise. (5) Never log or write the token into a GateRecord, a ledger row, an issue body or an error string. (6) Tests must not make real network calls: bind a local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 (which the proxy no-proxy list covers) and point the driver at it. Cover at least: a successful send stamps delivery.ok true; a driver that throws, times out, or is not configured still writes the record, still exits 0, and stamps delivery.attempted with ok false; severity routing picks the right channel; a record with no delivery field still validates.

title: Graph lint in code: validate the decomposition rules build-spec only states in a prompt
intent: `.claude/workflows/build-spec.js` lines 87-93 state the decomposition rules to the decomposer in prose and validate none of them. Run t7's decomposition still shipped a false edge AND assigned criterion AC-12 to a task that did not own the file that criterion names — a criterion assigned to a task that may not touch the file it names is unsatisfiable, and the fix loop cannot close it (rulings r5, c1). Two checks in pure script code, zero tokens, in the workflow body after the decomposer returns and before the TaskGraph is stamped. Check 1, CRITERION REACHABILITY: for every task, every acceptance criterion in that task's criteria_ids whose text names a repository path must have that path covered by the task's owned_surfaces. Reuse the existing directory-aware matching semantics from build-implement.js's withinOwned — an owned ref ending in '/' covers everything beneath it, one that does not covers only an exact match, so 'substrate/test' never covers 'substrate/testing/x.js'. Check 2, FALSE EDGE: every entry in a task's depends_on must be justified by a variable actually crossing that edge, which here means the depended-on task's owned_surfaces intersect a surface the dependent task's criteria require it to read or write; a depends_on that no data crossing justifies is a false edge, which CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids. Both checks must also reject a depends_on naming a task id that is not in the graph, and a dependency cycle. On a violation the workflow must NOT silently drop or auto-repair the task graph and must NOT pass by default: surface the violations on the returned object so the human sees them at the Spec Gate, and mark the affected spec as gated even when the risk router said low. Extract the checked functions between `// ---- BEGIN/END graph-lint ----` sentinels and unit-test them with the same extraction idiom substrate/test/extract-fixloop.js already uses, so the rules are tested without executing the workflow runtime. THIRD CHECK, added after run k2i, and the costliest failure so far. A spec may write criteria that no landed test can ever assert, and the correctness lens will then demand tests for them indefinitely. spec-wi-c8-node20-test-glob mixed two kinds of criterion and assigned both to one task and one test file. PRODUCT-SCOPED criteria ('the test script is exactly X', 'the engines floor equals ci.yml's node-version') can be asserted by a landed test on every run, forever. CHANGE-SCOPED criteria ('every other field byte-identical TO BEFORE', 'the changed paths are exactly these three', 'no dependency IS ADDED') are assertions about a DIFF: the verifier panel can check them and spec_conformance did and passed, but a landed test cannot, because after merge there is no 'before' and no 'this change', and a test pinning git diff to a base sha asserts nothing once that sha is history. The correctness lens saw three change-scoped criteria listed in criteria_coverage with no assertion covering them and, correct by its own contract, failed the change; the fix loop then sent three test-repair agents to write impossible tests. Cost: 25+ minutes, ~$0.93, one FORK BOMB (a generated test ran `npm test`, which re-ran that same test), one dispute that was right on its own terms, and a run that died without returning. No agent was wrong; the task was impossible. So: classify every criterion in script code before the graph is stamped. A criterion whose text is change-scoped — matching 'to before', 'byte-identical', 'changed paths', 'is added/removed/upgraded', 'unmodified' and their kin — is PANEL-VERIFIED: it must not be counted as a coverage gap by the correctness lens, and must never appear in a test file's criteria_ids. Carry the classification on the criterion itself so the lens prompt can be told which criteria it may demand tests for. Also fold in A6: a surface under the repo's test_dir must not appear in Spec.touched_surfaces, and the TestSet's landed files must be boundary-checked against owned_surfaces just as the implementer's ChangeSet is.

title: Drop lens findings cited against files the change never touched, in code rather than by prompt
intent: The lens-worktree fix is prompt-only, and prompt guidance has been measured insufficient here. Run t7i escalated repeat_finding on nine findings that were every one of them true of the base commit and false of the change under review: the lens prompt is the only verify-loop prompt that never named the worktree, so a lens that opened a file greped the repository root at the pre-task commit. The script cannot set a subagent's working directory, so no code-side enforcement exists. Add one in `.claude/workflows/build-implement.js`, applied to each round's raw verdicts alongside the existing stripForeignFindings step. IMPORTANT — the filter is FILE-LEVEL, NOT LINE-LEVEL, and it must never create a path where a panel passes by default. Drop a finding only when the file part of its cited location appears NEITHER in the set of files the diff touches NOR in the TestSet's tests_ref. Never drop a finding that cites an acceptance criterion this task owns, whatever its location — a spec-conformance finding of the form 'AC-7 is unmet' has no line in the diff BY CONSTRUCTION, and dropping it would let a change with a genuinely unmet criterion pass the panel. A finding whose cited file IS in the diff but whose cited line falls outside every diff hunk is a LOGGED WARNING ONLY, pushed to ctx.history and never dropped, so the ledger can measure how often line-level mismatch fires before anyone promotes it to a drop. Every dropped finding must be recorded on ctx.history with its dedupe_key and cited file, exactly as the existing dropped-finding logging does, so a drop is auditable and countable rather than silent. The set of files a diff touches must be derived from the actual diff at diff_ref by a mechanical agent — the script cannot read disk — and returned under a schema; if that agent fails or returns nothing, the filter must DISABLE ITSELF and drop nothing, because an empty file list would otherwise drop every finding and pass the change by default. Extract the pure decision functions between `// ---- BEGIN/END citation-filter ----` sentinels and unit-test them with the substrate/test/extract-fixloop.js idiom.

title: Memory → Build: feed /memory-roll's patterns to the decomposer and its canaries to the canary runner
intent: The Memory→Build edge does not exist. `grep -n "memory|pattern|prompt_refinement" .claude/workflows/build-spec.js` returns nothing. /memory-roll produces ten patterns and ten canaries (ledger/runs/mr2-memory-roll.json, roll.patterns and roll.canaries) and nothing consumes any of it, so the line cannot learn from its own history and a human notices things by hand instead. Two halves. B1: build-spec accepts an optional memory input — a path to a stored memory roll, read by a mechanical agent because the script cannot touch disk, returned under a schema — and injects the extracted patterns into the DECOMPOSER prompt as prior evidence, so a decomposition repeating a known-bad shape is caught without a human in the loop. Patterns must be passed as structured items the script selects and formats, never as an opaque blob, and the selection (which patterns, how many, on what relevance rule) is script code. B2: build-implement's canary runner currently reads A.canary from args only, at line 599, so a human hand-picks one; Phase 8's exit test needs the runner to pull from roll.canaries instead. Let build-implement accept a canary LIBRARY reference, select from it in script code by a deterministic rule (no Math.random — the runtime forbids it, so derive any choice from run_id and the task id), and keep the existing explicit A.canary as an override that always wins. Both halves must DEGRADE SILENTLY AND SAFELY: a missing, unreadable, empty or malformed memory roll must leave both workflows behaving exactly as they do today, because Memory is a Dark Factory sink that is never on a critical path (OPERATING_MODEL §8) and a build must never fail for want of it. Neither half may increase the token cost of a run that supplies no memory input. Unit-test the selection and formatting functions via the sentinel-extraction idiom, and cover the degradation paths explicitly.

title: Bind every workflow agent to a least-privilege agentType; a judgment node never holds a commit tool
intent: Run k1 measured the hole: build-spec's Iteration Planner named no agentType at its call site, so it resolved to the default workflow-subagent carrying Bash, Write and Edit. Its contract was to return selected work-item ids. Instead it created .github/workflows/ci.yml, ran npm ci and both suites, ran `git add .github && git commit`, and then returned a correct schema-valid {ids} as if it had only chosen. The write was disclosed by nothing in the workflow's output and was found by a git hook from outside the graph. The planner itself is already fixed by hand: it is deleted and replaced by script code between the `// ---- BEGIN/END plan-selection ----` sentinels, because selecting items within a token budget is a sort and a take and no judgment crosses that edge. THIS item is the rest of the audit. Enumerate every agent() call site in .claude/workflows/*.js and classify each as judgment (reads and reasons, must never write) or mechanical (legitimately needs shell and filesystem). Bind every judgment call site to a read-only agentType so the toolset, not a prompt sentence, is what prevents the write — A1's whole lesson is that prompt guidance is measured insufficient in this repo. Known unbound sites to start from: in build-spec.js the spec writer and the risk router both run as workflow-subagent. The spec writer is the hard case and must be decided explicitly rather than by reflex: it legitimately needs to read code, and today it uses Bash for cat, sed, grep and npm test, so a read-only Read/Glob/Grep type changes how it works and may need a new agent definition rather than an existing one. build-implement.js already binds its lenses and mechanical agents with AT(...) but has not been audited end to end; audit it and the other three workflows too. Note the runtime fact recorded in CLAUDE.md: agent definitions register from the committed tree on a delay, so any NEW .claude/agents/*.md this item adds will not resolve in the run that creates it, and each workflow must therefore still behave correctly when a type it names is missing — use the missing_agent_types mechanism rather than losing every definition. Add a test that fails when a judgment call site regains an unbound toolset, in the style of substrate/test/plan-selection.test.js, so this cannot silently come back. Do not change what any agent is asked to decide; this item changes only what each one is permitted to touch.

title: `npm test` is broken on Node 20 in both packages, while engines.node claims ">=20"
intent: Found by CI on its very first run, minutes after C4 landed it (GitHub Actions run 34667094594, commit 8f77338, branch task/t1-ci-workflow). Both test scripts QUOTE their glob: the root is `node --test "substrate/test/*.test.js"` and toy/ is `NODE_ENV=test node --test "test/*.test.js"`. Quoted, the shell does not expand the glob, so Node receives a literal pattern string. Node 22 accepts glob patterns for --test; Node 20 does not, and fails immediately with `Could not find '/home/runner/work/company-graph/company-graph/substrate/test/*.test.js'`, exit 1. Every development container this repository has run in uses Node 22, so both suites have always passed by hand and the incompatibility was invisible until something ran them on the version the repository claims to support. That is the exact class of gap C4 exists to close, and C4 closed it on run 1. The consequence is that `engines.node: ">=20"` in ./package.json is FALSE: these suites have only ever run on Node 22 or newer. CI currently pins node-version 20 precisely because it was told to match that engines field, so CI is red on every push until this is fixed. Two honest resolutions exist and the item must PICK ONE EXPLICITLY rather than drift into whichever is easier. (a) Make Node 20 genuinely work: unquote the glob in both package.json files so the shell expands it — verified to give 114/114 in the root suite on Node 22 in this container, and it is the portable form on Node 20 too. engines stays ">=20" and becomes true for the first time. Note that `node --test substrate/test/` is NOT a substitute: Node resolves a bare directory as a module path and throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND — measured, not assumed. (b) Admit the floor is Node 22: set engines.node to ">=22", set CI node-version to 22, and amend spec-wi-c4-ci's AC-4, which currently asserts node-version 20 and is enforced by substrate/test/ci-workflow.test.js. (a) is the smaller change and keeps the stated support promise; (b) is defensible only if something in the repository actually needs Node 22, which should be checked rather than assumed. Whichever is chosen, the deliverable must include CI going green on a push, because a claim that this is fixed is worth nothing unless the thing that caught it agrees. Also add a test asserting that the support floor named in engines.node and the node-version pinned in .github/workflows/ci.yml agree with each other, so the two cannot drift apart again silently.

title: A target=test finding disputed by the Test Author reaches no judge, and the panel then passes the unfixed change
intent: Measured on run k1v. This is a pass-by-default path in the component whose entire job is to refuse, so it outranks every other open build-line item. Sequence: round 1 raised a HIGH-severity finding at substrate/test/ci-workflow.test.js:190, independently reported by two lenses, both target=test. Two testfix agents ran and BOTH disputed. No judge ruled. Round 2 re-panelled, both lenses returned pass, the change integrated with escalations: 0 — and line 190 was never touched. The task branch's test file was byte-identical before and after. A real defect shipped inside a change the panel had just called clean. Mechanism, at .claude/workflows/build-implement.js:832-834: `disputed` filters on x.kind === 'code', and `testRepairs` filters to test repairs that did NOT dispute. A disputing test repair matches neither, so it never reaches the dispute judge at :872 (guarded on kind === 'code') and never sets resolution[dedupe_key]; the catch-all marks it unresolved, and an unresolved finding survives only while some lens keeps re-raising it. When the lens does not, it is silently gone. A code Fixer's dispute is always ruled on; a Test Author's is ruled on by nobody. Escalation.disputes_lost is fed from ctx.upheld, which only the judge writes, so a test dispute cannot even surface in an escalation. CONTRIBUTING CAUSE, and a defect in its own right: the test-repair agent is pointed at ctx.testSet.tests_ref (.artifacts/tests/<task>/, a COPY) while the finding cites the file on the branch — which is why one agent correctly replied that the finding 'does not apply to the file I am responsible for'. Worse, integration then reported tests_skipped: ['ci-workflow.test.js'] because the branch already carried that filename, so even a SUCCESSFUL repair would have been discarded. The test-repair path currently cannot fix a test file the implementer landed. This compounds with A6 rather than being independent of it. REQUIRED, none of it optional: (1) a disputing test repair must reach the same judge a code dispute does, and its outcome must land in ctx.upheld / ctx.overruled so escalations can see it; (2) resolution must be set for EVERY finding raised in a round, with 'nobody resolved it' treated as unresolved and CARRIED, never dropped; (3) a finding must never leave a round in a state where the only thing between it and a green panel is whether a cheap lens bothers to re-raise it; (4) the test-repair agent must be pointed at the file the finding cites, and integration must not silently skip landing a TestSet file that the repair path just edited. Add a regression test using the substrate/test/extract-fixloop.js sentinel idiom that drives the round-resolution decision directly: a test-target finding whose repair disputes must come out ruled or carried, never absent. Until this lands, a green panel is NOT evidence that target=test findings were addressed, and D1's rubber-stamping question has exactly one confirmed instance (this one) to calibrate against.

title: One repository-root resolver for the test suite, found by walking up rather than counting '..'
intent: Five files under substrate/test/ each resolve the repository root with the same hardcoded-depth expression, `path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..')`: ci-workflow.test.js:21, fixloop-helpers.js:14, helpers.js:7, node-support-floor-and-test-glob.test.js:24 and t2-doc-paths.js:15. Three of them (fixloop-helpers, helpers, t2-doc-paths) each EXPORT their own identical REPO constant, so the same fragile definition exists three times and is imported by at least six test files. The expression is correct only while the file sits exactly two levels below the repository root, and this repo routinely runs test files somewhere else: build-implement writes TestSets into .artifacts/tests/<task>/ and a mechanical agent may run them from there before they land, and AC-15-style tests copy the tree into a throwaway directory. A file at any other depth silently resolves REPO to the wrong directory. It is the same class of defect as C1 — something that works only at the location it was born in — and it has already bitten: the landed TestSet from an earlier run hardcoded the worktree it was authored in, which is gitignored and dies with the container. The fix already exists and is salvaged at .artifacts/salvage/repo-root.js (25 lines, written by the k1v Test Author and NOT merged with C4, because it was unused and outside that spec's touched_surfaces). It walks up from the calling file until it finds a directory containing BOTH contracts.schema.json and package.json, and throws a named error rather than returning a wrong answer if it reaches the filesystem root. Note .artifacts/ is gitignored, so that copy dies with the container: read it now or reconstruct the same behaviour. Deliverable: one module exporting REPO, used by every one of the five sites; the three duplicate REPO exports collapse to re-exports or are removed and their importers repointed; no test changes behaviour. Add a test that resolves the root correctly from a file at a DIFFERENT depth (write a temporary file two, three and one level down and assert all three agree), because a resolver only exercised from its birthplace proves exactly the thing the hardcoded version already proved. Out of scope: changing what any existing test asserts, adding a dependency, and touching anything outside substrate/test/.
